meta_description_en: Outlet #080 letters section: John Chapman asks about porting Tasword 2 to ZX Spectrum +3 disc and printer setup, with a step-by-step reply from Brian Cavers.
meta_description_ru: Рубрика писем Outlet #080: вопрос Джона Чепмена о переносе Tasword 2 на диск ZX Spectrum +3 и настройке принтера 8056, пошаговый ответ Брайана Каверса.
body_en_plain:
April, 1994       Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 John Chapman.........03    06

 Fred Ridout..........16    17

 Chris Ingram.........18    19

 W. Arnold Yates......22    23

 Brian Cavers.........27     -

 Barry Edgeway........30    31

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From John Chapman, NOTTINGHAM

Dear Brian and Ron,

I have enjoyed OUTLET for the
short time I have received it
and look forward to the next
months' issues. Here are a few
problems I have encounted.

I have a Serial 8056 compact
printer and I am unable to print
a screen display. It will print
out a listing after inputting...

FORMAT LINE 1200
FORMAT LPRINT "R"
LLIST
       ...but I can't enter this
if the program is in 48K as with
the Tasword 2 I have.


I would also like to put the
Tasword Two onto +3 disc for
speed and convenience. I can't
even save the text files to
disc. Maybe these problems have
been covered in past Outlets but
as a new reader I may have
missed them.


If the problems can be resolved
you had better explain "the
right hand margin set at 32" if
it's different to the standard
Tasword text.


I need simple, straightforward
instructions as most computer
instructions expect you to be
Brain of Britain.


When making up a video title the
screen can be a bit fuzzy.
Likewise the recording (I use a
standard TV as a monitor). Is
there anything, an electronic
circuit or add-on, to make the
screen clearer.

     Yours in anticipation,

         John Chapman

Brian Cavers to John Chapman


I have never tried to convert
Tasword 2 to +3 before but I
have just had a go and it seems
to run OK in 128K with one or
two provisos. If anyone else has
done this conversion and knows
of any other problems then let
us know please. This is what I
did...

1. Have a disc ready with room
for Tasword 2 (about 20K) but
DON'T put any disc in the drive
yet.

2. Reset the +3 and press ENTER
to prepare to load from tape in
128K mode.


3. Play the Tasword 2 tape and
load it. It should load and go
straight into the text editor as
normal.

4. Press SYMBOL plus A to go to
the Tasword 2 menu.

5. Press B then ENTER. Don't
press ENTER too firmly, release
it quickly. Don't press it again
or you are likely to select the
LOADER option on the 128K menu
and before you know it you may
be in load mode again. What I do
is press CURSOR DOWN, the 128K
loader menu should appear and
the highlight move down from
LOADER to +3 BASIC. You can now
press ENTER to get into BASIC!
Just BREAK if it goes wrong!


6. You should see the listing
and you should be at the top.
Move the flashing cursor down to
line 15 and move it to the start
of the line between the 15 and
the first command.

7. Enter FORMAT LPRINT "R":
FORMAT LINE 1200 : (make sure
you put in the colons).

8. Cursor along and down to the
LOAD command. I no longer have
an exact original but I think it
says LOAD "tasword" CODE. Change
"tasword" or whatever name is in
there to "TAS2.C" or any name
you prefer. I think the original
used the name "tasword" both for
the BASIC and the CODE which is
OK on tape but not on disc.


9. Alter line 710 to...

710 CLS: SAVE "TAS2.C" CODE
    54784,10751

                 ...or whatever
name you put in at line 15.

10. Alter line 700 to...

CLS : SAVE "TASWORD2" LINE 15

           ...or any name you
like but not the same as the one
at line 710. If you want Tasword
2 to boot in automatically from
the 128K menu loader then use
the word "DISK".

11. Delete line 780 (see next
page)


I have been assuming you know
how to edit and delete lines of
BASIC in 128K. You press ENTER
after any changes. To delete you
move the cursor BELOW a line and
just type the line number to be
deleted and press ENTER. In this
above case in No.11 on the page
before this you type 780 and
then ENTER.

12. Enter...
             790 GO TO 25

The VERIFY command doesn't work
on a +3 disc.

13. Delete line 1100

14. Enter...
              1110 GO TO 25


15. Put your disc in drive A and
I would be tempted to enter
SAVE "TEMP" to save the BASIC in
case anything goes wrong.You can
delete it later.


16. RUN the program and again
press SYMBOL plus A to get to
the Tasword 2 menu. This time
select T and then ENTER and it
should save the whole program to
disc.


I don't have a serial printer
connected to my +3 so I cannot
test this but let me know if
there is any problem printing or
if anyone else knows of some-
thing I have overlooked.


The only other problem I can see
is that you must NOT use REPLACE
and FIND mode because this uses
the addresses now used by the
128K system variables.Apart from
that it should be OK.

To set the right margin to 32,
go to the Tasword 2 text editor
(press Y and ENTER at the Tas2
menu). Move the cursor to the
right and you will see the col-
umn number increasing in the
info bar at the bottom of the
screen where it says Col. Stop
when it gets to 32. Press the
EXTEND MODE key and then D and
you should see the right side of
the screen go yellow. That is
the right margin. Cursor back to
the start and type!


You don't say how you are making
your video titles. I imagine you
may be simply plugging your TV
lead from your +3 in the aerial
input of your video. You really
need a direct video link.

First, look in the handbook of
your video recorder and see if
it describes the type of socket
used for video input on your
particular machine or you may
already know or can tell by
looking at the back of the
machine. I know of about five
different types...

BNC is a single central pin and
outer shield with a sort of
lockable collar to which you
give a half-twist.


SCART is an elongated rectangle
with one end at an angle and
with lots of pinholes.

There is one like a giant aerial
socket - the plug having a screw
collar - I don't know the name
off-hand.

There is the tiny single pin
like an audio phono socket or
the Spectrum tv.

Then there is the type on your
+3 which is a bit like a dyn
socket I think with several pins
in a circle.

Ring Meedmore Distribution on
051 521 2202 who, I understand,
make up leads to order.


Describe the two connections you
need. It is likely they will
know the +3 and they certainly
know all the various types. They
should be able to make up a lead
for you and this will give you a
much clearer signal.

                      Brian

From Fred Ridout, SWINDON

Dear Brian,

The following listing gives the
free space left on the silicon
RAM disc on a Spectrum +2...
[see recent reader's query]

10 LET sdm = PEEK 23430*256+
   PEEK 23429

20 IF PEEK 23431=1 THEN LET sdm
   = sdm + 65535

30 CLS : PRINT "MEM LEFT = ";sdm
   '"MEM USED = ";76779-sdm

             Yours,

               Fred

Brian Cavers to Fred Ridout



Brilliant, Fred! Many thanks. I
think the 65535 should strictly
be 65536 but what's one byte?!

The whole thing can be simpli-
fied to...


PRINT PEEK 23429 + PEEK 23430 *
256 + PEEK 23431 * 65536


                   Brian

From Chris Ingram, MALAWI

Dear Brian,

Your remarks on file corruption
on the Disciple are very
worrying: do you think this is
due to the Disciple's age or is
it a fault it's had all along?
I've had the odd file corrupt
before but never on the scale of
the time I told you about.

Following up my brief scribbled
note about my Masterfile merging
problems it occured to me that
you might be better able to
assist me if you could see the
files concerned. [sent]

         Chris Ingram


Brian Cavers to Chris Ingram

You should have my reply by now.

I regret my MASTERFILE merge has
overlooked the fact that there
are two flags marking records:
selected and unselected!My merge
only looks for selected!It never
occurred to me that anyone would
save a data file with unselected
files. I always keep all files
selected. I can then examine the
file in general at any time but
can also do a selected search.If
you keep all files unselected
you can do nothing until you
select some or all of them. In
other words, I can see no
advantage in leaving a file with
unselected records.


Nevertheless, that does not
excuse my oversight and I should
have provided for it. It is
theoretically possible to alter
my code to do the extra check
but I am reluctant because I
only just squeezed it in with
the MASTERFILE code.


POKE 57118,128 should make the
merge routine check for unsel-
ected instead of selected but
not both. The check is only to
find the start of the records in
the file - not to find each rec-
ord. If you had some selected
and some not I guess my routine
would find the first selected
one and merge all the ones after
that!


Anyway, I urge all users of my
merge routine to make sure they
have all records SELECTED in the
file that is being merged. It
does not matter about the file
that is already in memory.

You might like to read Malcolm
Perry's letter this month on
disc corruption - it may throw
more light on the problem.

                     Brian

From W.A. Yates, CHORLEY

I wonder if you can help me with
a slight problem, i.e. I have a
program called FOLIO, which is
used to keep track of stocks and
shares. It works OK on 48K+ with
Interface 1 and microdrive and I
can load and save to cartridge
with no problems. Although I can
transfer the program to Plus D
disk and it runs, it will not
work as it will not save the
data to disk.

I have been told if I alter line
Nos. 4663, 4667, 4773 and 4777,
the program will work. Can you
tell me what to type in, please?

             W.A. Yates


Ron Cavers to W.A. Yates

The lines you have indicated are
used to set up, and read to and
from, OPENTYPE files.

The first thing to be aware of
is that the CLOSE # statement
suffers from a bug in the Spec-
trum ROM. This was cured by MGT
in GDOS and a * has to be
entered to force it to their
routine - i.e. CLOSE #*S (S
being the stream number).

The Plus D handbook says their
command OPEN #;D1;"NAME" can
have the keywords IN or OUT
added (according to whether you
want to Input (IN) or Print
(OUT) to the file.


However, if IN or OUT are not
specified, it will default to IN
if an existing file of that name
is in the catalogue and OUT if
not.

I have never been able to get
this command in without adding
IN or OUT, so the lines need to
read:


4663 CLOSE #*4: OPEN #4;"m";1;f$
OUT : etc

4667 CLOSE #*4 :etc

4773 CLOSE #*4: OPEN #4;"m";1;f$
IN : etc

4777 CLOSE #*4 : etc


Note that the PRINT #4 and INPUT
#4 statements do not need to be
altered.

The microdrive syntax can be
changed to that of the Plus D
but I have left it as it is as
you then only have to edit the
relative lines and add the *'s
and an IN and OUT. (IN and OUT
being the keywords on the I and
O keys in the Spectrum extended
mode).

The program can then be saved to
disk by typing, as a direct
command:


CLEAR: SAVE D1;"FOLIO" LINE 10



The program should now work OK -
drop us another line if you
still have any problems.

                        Ron

Brian Cavers to Disciple/+D'ers!

I found a wierd bug which may
have been mentioned before in
OUTLET...

10 INPUT A$
20 DIM B$(100)
30 SAVE D1"TEST.D"DATA B$()

Look OK doesn't it? It does a
reset on mine! I don't know at
this time if it is a DOS bug or
what. I am using Betados. The
cure took me ages of head-
banging and primal screaming to
find because my program was much
more complex than the above and
I had to keep stripping out bits
to leave the above. The answer
is... Wait for it!....


You need to use... No, you won't
believe me. Even I don't believe
me!

In the first hour I simply could
find no way to save data if an
INPUT had taken place (it didn't
matter about size or type of any
variables). Then I thought,
surely there must be OUTLET
programs that actually need to
INPUT the filename of the data
to be saved! I thought and
thought - Eureka! MASTERFILE
does it OK all the time! So, I
examined MASTERFILE for another
hour. I could see no difference
to my program which reset yet MF
did not! Finally, I spent an
hour stripping each program line
by line until only three lines
remained...

These are, in essence, what was
left...

10 INPUT A$
20 DIM B$(100)
30 SAVE D1"TEST.D"DATA B$()

10 INPUT A$
20 DIM B$(100)
30 SAVE d1"TEST.D"DATA B$()

Yet the first one resets the
machine; the second one doesn't!
I stared in incredulity. Surely
it can't be... Naw! Well, did
you spot it? Yes, the little "d"
in the SAVE d1 is the only diff-
erence - and that is sufficient
to crash the system! The moral
is: "ALWAYS USE A LITTLE d, SON,
OR A LOONY YOU WILL BECOME!"
                          Brian

From Barry Edgeway, NORWICH

Dear Brian,

Many thanks for your assistance
regarding the problem with SPEC-
FILE and the thought you put
into it. (OUTLETTERS 77).

Unfortunately your tips did not
work which was not surprising as
you had nothing to work on. I
enclose a working copy of SPEC-
FILE and would be most grateful
if you could take a look to see
if you can get a chosen word to
highlight after a search.

       Yours sincerely,

         Barry Edgeway

Brian Cavers to all SPECFILERS!

I made a simple mod which, while
a bit slow(it can be skipped any
time with a keypress) highlights
ALL occurrences of the selected
word in SPECFILE...

315 POKE 23560,0 : FOR Y=1 TO 16

316 FOR X=1 TO 32

317 IF E$(Y,X)=X$(1) THEN
    FOR J=1 TO LEN X$-1:
 IF E$(Y,X+J)=X$(J+1)THEN NEXT J
 :PRINT BRIGHT 1;FLASH 1;OVER 1;
 AT Y-1,X-1;" "(TO LEN X$ :

318 NEXT X

319IF NOT PEEK 23560 THEN NEXT Y
                     - Brian.

Я никогда раньше не пробовал пре-
образовывать Tasword 2 для +3, но
сейчас попробовал, и вроде бы все

Если кто-то еще делал такую конвер-
сию и знает о каких-либо пробле-
мах, сообщите нам. Вот что я сде-
лал...

1. Подготовьте диск с местом для

2. Сбросьте +3 и нажмите ENTER для

3. Включите кассету с Tasword 2 и
загрузите его. Он должен загрузить-
ся и сразу перейти в текстовый ре-

4. Нажмите SYMBOL + A, чтобы перей-
ти в меню Tasword 2.

5. Нажмите B, а затем ENTER. Не на-
жимайте ENTER слишком сильно, отпус-
кайте быстро. Не нажимайте его еще
раз, иначе вы можете выбрать опцию
LOADER в меню 128K, и сами не заме-
тите, как окажетесь в режиме загруз-
ки. Я делаю так: нажимаю CURSOR
DOWN, меню загрузчика 128K должно
появиться, и подсветка переместится
с LOADER на +3 BASIC. Теперь можно
нажать ENTER, чтобы войти в BASIC!
Просто нажмите BREAK, если что-то
пойдет не так!

6. Вы должны увидеть листинг, вы
должны быть в его начале. Переме-
стите мигающий курсор вниз к строке
15 и поставьте его в начало строки
между числом 15 и первой командой.

7. Введите:

```text
FORMAT LPRINT "R": FORMAT LINE 1200 :
```
(убедитесь, что поставили двоеточия).

8. Переместитесь курсором вниз к ко-

написано LOAD "tasword" CODE. Изме-
ните "tasword" или любое другое имя
на "TAS2.C" или любое имя, которое
предпочитаете. Думаю, оригинал ис-
пользовал имя "tasword" и для BASIC,
и для CODE, что нормально для ленты,
но не для диска.

```text
710 CLS: SAVE "TAS2.C" CODE 54784,10751
```

которое вы вписали в строке 15.

10. Измените строку 700 на...


710. Если хотите, чтобы Tasword 2
автоматически загружался из меню
128K, используйте слово "DISK".

11. Удалите строку 780 (см. следую-
щую страницу).

Я исхожу из того, что вы знаете,
как редактировать и удалять строки

ний нажимайте ENTER. Чтобы удалить,

сто введите номер удаляемой строки

11 на странице ранее, вы вводите
780 и затем ENTER.

12. Введите...
```text

```
Команда VERIFY на диске +3 не рабо-
тает.

13. Удалите строку 1100.

14. Введите...
```text
1110 GO TO 25
```

удалить.

Ron Cavers — W.A. Yates

Строки, которые вы указали, исполь-
зуются для настройки и чтения из
файлов типа OPENTYPE.

Первое, о чем нужно знать: опера-
тор CLOSE # страдает от ошибки в
ПЗУ Spectrum. Это было исправлено
MGT в GDOS, и нужно вводить * ,
чтобы принудительно направить его
на их подпрограмму — т.е. CLOSE #*S
(S — номер потока).

В руководстве к Plus D сказано, что
их команда OPEN #;D1;"NAME" может
иметь ключевые слова IN или OUT (в
зависимости от того, хотите ли вы
считывать (IN) или записывать (OUT)
в файл).

Однако, если IN или OUT не указаны,
система по умолчанию выберет IN,
если существующий файл с таким
именем есть в каталоге, и OUT, если
нет.

Мне никогда не удавалось ввести эту
команду без добавления IN или OUT,
поэтому строки должны выглядеть
так:

```text
4663 CLOSE #*4: OPEN #4;"m";1;f$ OUT : etc
4667 CLOSE #*4 : etc
4773 CLOSE #*4: OPEN #4;"m";1;f$ IN : etc
4777 CLOSE #*4 : etc
```

Обратите внимание, что операторы
PRINT #4 и INPUT #4 изменять не
нужно.

Синтаксис Microdrive можно изменить на синтаксис Plus D, но я оставил всё как есть, так как вам останется лишь отредактировать соответствующие строки и добавить звёздочки (*), а также IN и OUT (IN и OUT — это ключевые слова на клавишах I и O в расширенном режиме Spectrum).

Затем программу можно сохранить на диск, введя прямую команду:

```text
CLEAR: SAVE D1;"FOLIO" LINE 10
```

Теперь программа должна работать нормально — напишите нам снова, если у вас всё ещё возникнут какие-либо проблемы.

                        Ron
